citation: Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the Earliest Period to the Present Time. Vol. 3, From the Fire of 1871 until 1885. Chicago: A. T. Andreas, 1886.
author: Alfred Theodore Andreas
locator: Local Transportation, pp. 164-166: the North Chicago Railway's lines 'constructed entire since the fire', among them 'two and one-fifth miles of double track on Wells Street from Randolph to North Clark, by November, 1875'; the West Division company's losses in the fire, its tracks 'east of the river' and its offices on State Street.
rights_note: Published 1886 in the United States; public domain.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-27 (T-3806) from the Internet Archive's OCR text of this scan (historyofchicago03andruoft_djvu.txt), at the printed page numbers the OCR carries in its running heads; the page images were not opened.
note: Used for what the horse railways were NOT in October 1871: lines it records as built after the fire (Wells Street, Lincoln Avenue) are not laid in the 1871 scene.
what_it_supplies: the North Side horse-railway lines built after the fire, and their dates
the West Division Railway's fire losses (its tracks east of the river)
what_it_does_not_supply: the routes of 1871 themselves (vol. 2 and the 1871 directory give those)
